title: Ear anatomy: hearing and balance structures
description: A pressure-wave collector that turns vibration into nerve impulses and doubles as a gyroscope.

questions.question: How do the outer, middle and inner ear work together?
questions.answer: The outer ear collects sound, the eardrum and three middle-ear bones transmit vibration, and the cochlea in the inner ear converts movement into nerve signals.

questions.question: Which part of the ear helps with balance?
questions.answer: The vestibular organs of the inner ear, including the semicircular canals and otolith organs, detect head rotation and linear movement.

questions.question: What is the tympanic membrane?
questions.answer: A 9 × 10 mm cone of three layers, tilted so its umbo points medially; pars tensa below, pars flaccida above. Function: Converts sound pressure into mechanical vibration of the malleus.

questions.question: Where is the stapes located?
questions.answer: The stirrup: the smallest bone in the body (~3 mm), its footplate closing the oval window. Function: Delivers amplified vibration into the cochlear fluid.

questions.question: What is the function of the vestibule (utricle & saccule)?
questions.answer: Function: Sense linear acceleration and head tilt — gravity sensing. Two otolith organs whose hair cells carry crystals of calcium carbonate.
